column2: “Choose TWO letters” — aynan ikkita javob tanlang. Avval savol nimani so‘raganini belgilang, har variantni audio dalili bilan tekshiring, keyin ikki tanlov qolganini sanang. Misol: ikki qulaylik so‘ralsa, narx haqidagi gap uchinchi javob bo‘lib qolmaydi.
column3: “Choose TWO letters” requires exactly two selections. Identify the requested information, check each option against audio evidence, then count your selections. If two facilities are requested, a comment about price is not a third answer.

column2: “Choose THREE answers” — uchta javob kerak. Uchta tanlovning har biriga alohida dalil toping; shunchaki ketma-ket uch harfni olmang. Masalan, uch sabab so‘ralsa, sabab, natija va misolni bir xil deb hisoblamang.
column3: Choose exactly three supported answers. Find independent evidence for each; do not pick three consecutive letters. If the question asks for three causes, distinguish a cause from a consequence or an example.

column2: Variantlar sonidan emas, savol ustidagi yo‘riqnomadan biling: “Choose ONE”, “Choose TWO” yoki “Choose THREE”. Belgilashdan oldin shu sonni yozib oling, yuborishdan oldin tanlangan javoblarni sanang. Yo‘riqnoma ko‘rinmasa, taxmin qilishdan oldin uni tekshiring.
column3: Read the instruction, not the number of available options: Choose ONE, TWO or THREE. Note that number before listening and count selections before submitting. If the instruction is missing, check it rather than guessing.

column2: Ikki variantning farqini bitta jumlada yozing: vaqtmi, sababmi yoki kimning fikrimi? Audio aynan qaysi farqni tasdiqlaganini tekshiring. “Arzon” va “qulay joyda” bir narsani anglatmaydi; spiker narxni aytgan bo‘lsa, joy haqidagi javobni qo‘shmang.
column3: Write the difference between the two options: time, reason or speaker? Listen for evidence resolving that difference. Cheap and conveniently located are different claims; mentioning price does not establish location.

column2: Tuzatish aynan so‘ralgan ma’lumotga tegishli bo‘lsa, yakuniy tasdiqlangan shaklni oling. “Tuesday—sorry, Thursday”da Thursday qoladi. Lekin keyingi gap boshqa odam yoki boshqa rejaga tegishli bo‘lsa, birinchi javobni avtomatik almashtirmang.
column3: Use the final corrected information about the same requested fact. In “Tuesday—sorry, Thursday”, Thursday replaces Tuesday. A later sentence about a different person or plan does not automatically replace the earlier answer.

column2: NOT mentioned — aytilmaganini topish. Har variant uchun “aytildi” yoki “dalil yo‘q” deb tekshiring; noto‘g‘ri deb aytilgan bilan umuman aytilmagan farq qiladi. Savoldagi NOTni oldindan belgilang, keyin tanlovni qayta o‘qing.
column3: NOT mentioned asks for information absent from the recording. Mark which options have evidence. Explicit rejection differs from no mention at all. Highlight NOT before listening and reread the instruction before choosing.

column2: “Maybe”, “I thought” dastlabki taxmin bo‘lishi mumkin; “actually”, “in the end”, “we decided” yakuniy qarorni ko‘rsatishi mumkin. Belgining o‘ziga emas, undan keyingi to‘liq fikrga tayaning. Oldingi va oxirgi pozitsiyani ikki ustunda yozing.
column3: Separate initial hesitation from the final position. Maybe or I thought may introduce an early idea; actually or we decided may signal revision. Check the complete statement and whose view it is, not a signal word alone.

column2: Bir xil so‘z — dalilning o‘zi emas. Variantdagi butun da’voni: kim, nima, qachon va inkorni solishtiring. “We considered the bus but took the train”da bus eshitildi, ammo tanlangan transport train. Kalit so‘z emas, ma’no mos bo‘lishi kerak.
column3: An identical word is not enough. Compare the full claim, including person, time and negation. “We considered the bus but took the train” mentions bus, but train is the chosen transport. Match meaning rather than isolated words.

column2: Avval savolning nimani so‘rashini o‘qing, keyin variantlar orasidagi farqni belgilang. Uzun variantlarni qisqa tayanchlarga aylantiring. Audio davomida barcha matnni qayta o‘qishga urinmang; savol va asosiy farqni kuzating.
column3: Read the stem to identify the task, then compare the options. Reduce long choices to brief distinguishing notes. During playback, follow the requested information instead of repeatedly rereading every option.

column2: Har variantni 2–4 so‘zli ma’no tayanchiga qisqartiring: “price too high”, “location inconvenient”, “no weekend service”. Raqam, inkor va cheklovni saqlang. Tinglayotganda shu farqlarga dalil izlang, so‘zma-so‘z moslikka emas.
column3: Reduce each option to a short meaning cue, preserving numbers, negation and qualifiers: price too high, inconvenient location, no weekend service. Listen for the distinction rather than exact wording.

column2: O‘zingiz uchun ✓ — tasdiq, × — rad, ? — hali dalil yo‘q belgilarini ishlating. Yoniga qisqa sabab yozing: “too expensive”, “changed plan”. ? ni to‘g‘ri javob deb olmang; bu faqat hali tekshirilmagan variant.
column3: Use brief personal notes: ✓ supported, × rejected, ? unresolved. Add a short reason such as too expensive or changed plan. A question mark means insufficient evidence, not a correct answer.

column2: Xato variantni nega tanlaganingizni yozing, keyin audiodagi hal qiluvchi gap va to‘g‘ri variantning ma’nosini solishtiring. Xatoni “inkorni o‘tkazdim”, “eski qarorni oldim”, “bir xil so‘zga aldandim” deb nomlang. Keyingi urinishda shu turdagi dalilni qidiring.
column3: Record why you chose the wrong option, locate the decisive sentence, and compare its meaning with the correct choice. Label the error: missed negation, earlier decision or word matching. Practise detecting that error instead of memorising the key.

column2: Avval yo‘riqnomada bitta yoki ikki tanlov so‘ralganini tekshiring. Ikki javob aniq talab qilinib, ikkinchisi birinchisini o‘chirsa, bu interfeys xatosi bo‘lishi mumkin. Savol nomi, qurilma va ko‘rinadigan yo‘riqnoma bilan Supportga xabar bering; tugallanmagan javobni avval saqlang.
column3: Check whether the instruction requires one or two choices. If two are required but selecting the second clears the first, report a possible interface mismatch with the item, device and visible instruction. Preserve unfinished work before leaving.

column2: Topshirishdan oldin yangi variantni tanlang; ko‘p tanlovli savolda avval ortiqcha tanlovni olib tashlash talab qilinishi mumkin. Yuborishdan oldin saqlangan tanlovni qayta ko‘ring. Topshirilgan urinishni o‘zgartirish imkonini esa sahifadagi holat belgilaydi.
column3: Before submission, select the replacement; a multiple-selection item may require deselecting an extra choice first. Recheck the saved selection. Whether a submitted attempt can be changed depends on its actual state and controls.

column2: Savol ichida pastga suring, klaviaturani yoping va brauzer kattalashtirishini tekshiring. Javob tanlanganini ko‘rmasdan Submit bosmang. Variant yopilib qolsa, sahifa, telefon modeli va xato ko‘rinishini Supportga yuboring; yashirin variantni taxmin qilmang.
column3: Scroll within the question, dismiss the keyboard and check browser zoom. Confirm the selected option before submitting. If an option remains obscured, report the page and device with a screenshot rather than guessing an unseen choice.

column2: Harf nomlarini farqlang: B /biː/, D /diː/, P /piː/. P boshida havo kuchliroq chiqadi; B va Dning boshlang‘ich tovushi boshqa. Avval B–D, B–P juftlarini, keyin qisqa harflangan ismlarni yozib mashq qiling. Kontekst va qayta aytilgan spellingni tekshiring.
column3: Practise letter names B /biː/, D /diː/ and P /piː/. Their initial consonants differ; P often has a stronger puff of air. Start with pairs, then short spelled names, and verify using repeated spelling and context.

column2: Tuzatilgan raqamni faqat bir xil telefon raqamiga tegishli bo‘lsa almashtiring. “018—sorry, 081”da oxirgi uch raqam 081. Raqamlarni kichik guruhlarda yozing, tuzatilgan guruh ustidan belgilang va yakunida butun raqamni tekshiring.
column3: Replace only the corrected part of the same number. In “018—sorry, 081”, use 081 for that group. Write numbers in small chunks, mark the revised chunk and check the complete final number.

column2: Standart Listening yo‘riqnomasida well-known kabi defis bilan yozilgan so‘z bitta so‘z sanaladi. Lekin asl imloda defissiz ikki so‘zni limitga sig‘dirish uchun sun’iy birlashtirmang. Har safar aynan topshiriqning so‘z va raqam chegarasini tekshiring.
column3: In standard Listening instructions, a genuinely hyphenated word such as well-known counts as one word. Do not invent hyphens to squeeze unrelated words into the limit. Check the particular word and number instruction.

column2: Avval bo‘sh joydan oldin artikl allaqachon bormi, qarang. “a ___” uchun “a museum”ni yana to‘liq qo‘shish “a a museum” qiladi. Butun gapni javob bilan o‘qing, audio shakli, grammatika va word limitni birga tekshiring.
column3: Check whether the sentence already supplies the article. Adding “a museum” after “a ___” duplicates a. Read the completed sentence and verify the audio wording, grammar and word limit together.

column2: Birlik savolda tashqarida berilgan bo‘lsa, ko‘pincha bo‘sh joyga faqat son kerak: “___ kg” → “15”. Javobni butun qatorga qo‘yib tekshiring; “15 kg kg” bo‘lib qolmasin. Alohida answer field yo‘riqnomasini ham o‘qing.
column3: If the unit is already supplied, the blank often needs only the number: “___ kg” → 15. Read the completed line to avoid “15 kg kg”, and follow any separate answer-field instructions.

column2: Boshlanish nuqtasi va dastlabki qarash yo‘nalishini belgilang. Har burilishdan keyin hozirgi yurish yo‘nalishingizni yangilang: chap har doim qog‘ozning chap tomoni emas. Yo‘lni qisqa segmentlar bilan kuzating, mo‘ljal binolarda joyingizni tekshiring.
column3: Mark the start and initial facing direction. Update your orientation after every turn: left is relative to travel, not always the left side of the page. Trace short route segments and check landmarks.

column2: “You are here” boshlash nuqtasidir. Keyin audio qaysi tomonga yurishni aytganini aniqlang; xaritaning yuqori tomonini avtomatik oldinga deb olmang. Boshlanish, yo‘nalish va birinchi mo‘ljalni aniqlagach keyingi burilishlarni kuzating.
column3: Start at You are here, then establish the direction described in the audio. Do not assume the top of the map is forward. Identify the first landmark before tracking subsequent turns.

column2: Taklif va yakuniy tanlovni ajrating: “We could cycle, but it’s too far. Let’s take the bus.” Bu yerda cycle rad etilgan, bus tanlangan. “but”, sabab va keyingi kelishuvni birga eshiting; barcha tilga olingan variantlarni tavsiya deb olmang.
column3: Distinguish a suggestion from acceptance: “We could cycle, but it’s too far. Let’s take the bus.” Cycling is rejected; the bus is chosen. Follow the reason and agreement, not merely which options were mentioned.

column2: Ustun sarlavhasi va qo‘shni kataklarni tekshiring: “Date” sana, “Cost” narx, “Material” narsa nomini kutadi. Keyin grammatika orqali birlik/ko‘plik yoki so‘z turkumini tekshiring. Bu javobni oldindan uydirish emas, qaysi ma’lumotni tinglashni belgilashdir.
column3: Use column headings and neighbouring cells to predict the information type: date, cost or material. Grammar can indicate singular/plural or part of speech. Predict the category to listen for, not an invented answer.

column2: Strelka jarayonning keyingi bosqichini ko‘rsatadi; qatorlarni faqat chapdan o‘ngga o‘qimang. Boshlanishni topib, har tugundan keyingi strelkani kuzating. “After”, “then”, “finally”ni bosqich mazmuni bilan birga tekshiring.
column3: Follow arrows from the starting stage rather than assuming ordinary reading order. Track each node and the next arrow. Link after, then and finally to what actually happens at that stage.

column2: Har so‘zlovchiga qisqa alohida qayd oching. Bir kishi oldingi fikrini o‘zgartirsa, vaqt va savolda so‘ralgan pozitsiyani tekshiring. Variantni qayta ishlatish mumkinmi — yo‘riqnomadan biling; odam soni bilan fikrlar soni teng bo‘lishi shart emas.
column3: Keep separate notes for each speaker. If one changes opinion, check the time and position requested. Read whether an option may be reused; the number of speakers need not equal the number of views.

column2: Of ko‘pincha /əv/, to /tə/ kabi kuchsizlashadi. Uch mashq: “a cup of tea”, “I want to go”, “a lot of work”. Avval transkript bilan tinglang, keyin matnni yopib bo‘lakni yozing; so‘z yo‘qolgan emas, urg‘usizlashgan bo‘lishi mumkin.
column3: Of may weaken to /əv/ and to to /tə/. Practise a cup of tea, I want to go and a lot of work. Listen with the transcript, hide it and transcribe the chunk; unstressed words may be reduced rather than absent.

column2: O‘tgan javobga uzoq yopishib qolmang. Taxminiy belgi qo‘yib, navbatdagi savol tayanchiga ko‘zingizni qaytaring. Yozuvni qisqa tuting va keyin ruxsat etilgan tekshirish vaqtida imloni tuzating. Bitta bo‘sh javob sabab keyingi beshtasini yo‘qotmang.
column3: Mark the missed item and move to the next question cue instead of replaying it mentally. Use short notes and correct spelling during the permitted checking time. Avoid losing several later answers over one missed response.

column2: Savoldagi noyob ma’no yoki sinonimini transkriptdan toping, keyin oldingi va keyingi gapni o‘qing. Playerda shu joyni tinglab, qaysi so‘z javobni o‘zgartirganini belgilang. Men audio yoki timestamp berilmasa aniq sekundni uydirmayman.
column3: Locate the question’s idea or paraphrase in the transcript, read the surrounding sentences, then replay that section. Identify the decisive wording. Without the audio or timestamps, I cannot invent an exact second.

column2: Blank oldidagi a/an birlikni, many/several ko‘plikni kutishi mumkin; son va fe’l mosligini ham tekshiring. Misol: “three ___” → books. Oxirgi /s/ni audio bilan tekshiring: grammatik taxmin dalilning o‘rnini bosmaydi.
column3: An article may predict a singular noun; many, several or a number may predict plural. Check agreement and the audio ending: “three ___” suggests books. A grammatical prediction does not replace listening evidence.

column2: “All” hammasini, “some” ayrimlarini bildiradi. “Some students cycle” butun guruh velosipedda yurishini isbotlamaydi va qolganlar yurmasligini ham o‘zi isbotlamaydi. Qarama-qarshi dalil bo‘lmasa “all” haqidagi da’vo Not Given bo‘lishi mumkin; matnning qolgan qismini tekshiring.
column3: All covers the whole group; some does not establish all, but alone does not prove that the rest do not. “Some students cycle” therefore may leave an all claim Not Given. Check the full passage for confirming or contradicting evidence.

column2: “If X, Y” shartli fikr; uni shartsiz “Y doim bo‘ladi”ga aylantirmang. Muallif shartni zarur deb aytganmi yoki faqat bir holatni berganmi, tekshiring. Shart olib tashlangan gap avtomatik No emas: qarama-qarshilik bo‘lmasa Not Given bo‘lishi mumkin.
column3: “If X, Y” is conditional, not an unconditional Y. Check whether the author presents X as necessary or merely describes one case. Removing a condition is not automatically No; without contradiction, the claim may be Not Given.

column2: Paragrafga “Bu paragrafning butun maqsadi nima?” deb bir jumla yozing. Misol va qiziq sonlar shu fikrni qo‘llab-quvvatlaydi. Heading faqat bitta detalga emas, paragrafning katta qismiga mos kelishi kerak. Qarama-qarshi burilishdan keyingi xulosani ham tekshiring.
column3: Summarise the purpose of the whole paragraph in one sentence. Examples and striking figures usually support that point. A heading must cover the paragraph rather than one detail; check any contrast and concluding shift.

column2: Matching Informationda dalillar savol tartibida kelishi shart emas. Har banddagi noyob fikrni belgilang, matndan tegishli joyni qidiring va paragraf harfini qayd qiling. Bir javob topilgani keyingisi faqat undan keyinda bo‘ladi degani emas.
column3: Matching Information need not follow paragraph order. Identify each item’s distinctive idea, scan for its evidence and note the paragraph letter. Finding one answer does not mean the next must appear later.

column2: Bitta ismni qayta ishlatish mumkinligi yo‘riqnomaga bog‘liq. “You may use any letter more than once” bo‘lsa mumkin. Har tavsifni odam bilan alohida dalil orqali bog‘lang; bir marta ishlatilgani uchun ismni avtomatik o‘chirmang.
column3: Read the instruction about reusing letters. If it permits reuse, the same person can match several statements. Find evidence for each association; do not eliminate a name merely because you have already used it.

column2: Avval gapni grammatik tugating, keyin yakundagi da’voni matn bilan tekshiring. Grammatik moslik nomzodni qoldiradi, ammo to‘g‘rilikni isbotlamaydi. Sabab-natija, vaqt va kimga tegishli ekanini solishtirib, dalilsiz yakunni chiqaring.
column3: Check grammar first, then test the completed claim against the passage. Grammatical fit makes an option possible, not correct. Verify cause, time and participants and eliminate endings lacking textual evidence.

column2: Ortiqcha headinglar chalg‘ituvchi variantlardir; hammasi ishlatilishi shart emas. Har paragrafning asosiy vazifasini qisqa yozib, mos headingni tanlang. Qolgan headingni majburan moslamang; cheklovchi so‘zlarini qayta tekshiring.
column3: Extra headings are distractors and need not all be used. Summarise each paragraph’s main function before matching. Do not force an unused heading onto a paragraph; recheck its qualifiers.

column2: Blankning chap va o‘ng tomonini o‘qing. Artikldan keyin ot birikmasi, sifatdan keyin ot, modal fe’ldan keyin asosiy fe’l kelishi mumkin. Matndan tanlangan javobni qo‘yib butun note’ni o‘qing, imlo va limitni tekshiring.
column3: Read both sides of the gap. An article may introduce a noun phrase; a modal is followed by a base verb. Insert the passage wording into the complete note, then check grammar, spelling and the word limit.

column2: Avval sxemadagi boshlanish va strelkalarni kuzating. Har bosqichning kalit ma’nosini matndan mustaqil toping; bosqichlar turli paragrafda tasvirlangan bo‘lishi mumkin. Birinchi dalil joylashuvi keyingi bosqich joyini kafolatlamaydi.
column3: Trace the flow-chart’s start and arrows, then locate evidence for each stage independently. Stages may be described in different paragraphs. The position of one answer does not guarantee where the next appears.

column2: Word box bo‘lsa berilgan variantlardan tanlaysiz, javob ko‘pincha harf bilan belgilanadi — yo‘riqnomani tekshiring. Box bo‘lmasa odatda matndan so‘z olasiz va limitga rioya qilasiz. Har ikkala holatda ma’no va grammatika mos bo‘lishi kerak.
column3: With a word box, choose from the supplied options and follow whether letters are required. Without one, use passage words within the stated limit. In both cases, check the meaning and grammar of the completed summary.

column2: “NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER” ikki so‘zgacha, bitta raqam yoki ularning ruxsat etilgan birikmasini bildiradi: “red books”, “15”, “15 red books”. Uch so‘z chegaradan oshadi. Javobning aynan shu blankka mos ma’nosini ham tekshiring.
column3: It allows up to two words, a number, or the permitted combination: red books, 15, or 15 red books. Three words exceed the word allowance. The answer must still match the particular blank and its meaning.

column2: Raqamning qabul qilinishi aynan yo‘riqnomaga bog‘liq. “AND/OR A NUMBER” bo‘lsa raqam uchun alohida ruxsat bor; “ONE WORD ONLY”ni xohlagan raqam bilan chetlab o‘tmang. Raqam bilan yozilgan va so‘z bilan yozilgan sonni bir xil sanash deb taxmin qilmang.
column3: Follow the precise instruction. AND/OR A NUMBER provides a number allowance; do not use a numeral to bypass an unrelated ONE WORD ONLY instruction. Do not assume a numeral and a number written in words are counted identically.

column2: Matndan kerakli so‘zni to‘g‘ri imlo bilan oling. Atoqli otning bosh harfi, defis va apostrofni tekshiring; ortiqcha tinish belgisi qo‘shmang. Saytdagi avtomatik tekshiruv qanday normallashtirishini bilmasdan “har qanday imlo qabul qilinadi” deb bo‘lmaydi.
column3: Copy the required wording with correct spelling. Check proper-name capitals, hyphens and apostrophes; avoid unnecessary punctuation. Do not assume the website accepts every spelling or punctuation variation without checking its feedback.

column2: Bir paragraf bir nechta ma’lumotni berishi mumkin. Har savol uchun alohida dalil yozing va harfni qayta ishlatish yo‘riqnomasini o‘qing. Oldingi javobda ishlatilgan paragrafni avtomatik ro‘yxatdan chiqarish xato bo‘lishi mumkin.
column3: One paragraph can contain several requested facts. Find separate evidence for each and check the instruction on letter reuse. Automatically excluding an already used paragraph may produce an error.

column2: Birinchi gap yo‘nalish beradi, ammo keyingi “however” fikrni burishi mumkin. Birinchi gap, burilish va yakuniy fikrni birga o‘qing. Headingni tanlashdan oldin paragrafning umumiy maqsadini o‘z so‘zingiz bilan ayting.
column3: The first sentence is a clue, but a later however may change the focus. Read the opening, contrast and final point together. State the paragraph’s overall purpose before choosing its heading.

column2: “Buni matndagi qaysi gap isbotlaydi?” deb so‘rang. Hayotda mantiqli tuyulgan xulosa matnda berilgan bo‘lishi shart emas. Sabab, niyat yoki universal qoida matnda bo‘lmasa ularni qo‘shmang; dalil yo‘qligi qarama-qarshilikning o‘zi emas.
column3: Ask which sentence proves the claim. A plausible real-world inference is not necessarily stated by the passage. Do not add an unstated cause, intention or universal rule; lack of evidence alone is not contradiction.

column2: Inkor doirasini bosqichma-bosqich ajrating. “Not uncommon” — kamyob emas, ammo “always common” emas. “Not all failed” hech bo‘lmasa ayrimlari yiqilmaganini bildiradi; “none failed” bilan teng emas. So‘ng soddalashtirilgan ma’noni matn bilan solishtiring.
column3: Resolve the scope of each negative. Not uncommon is not the same as always common. Not all failed means at least some did not fail; it does not mean none failed. Compare the resulting meaning with the passage.

column2: They uchun oldingi ko‘plik otlarni, this uchun oldingi fikr yoki hodisani tekshiring. Olmosh o‘rniga nomzod iborani qo‘yib gapni qayta o‘qing. Eng yaqin ot doim to‘g‘ri emas; son, ma’no va gaplar orasidagi bog‘lanish mos bo‘lishi kerak.
column3: Check earlier plural noun phrases for they and preceding ideas or events for this. Substitute a candidate reference and reread. The nearest noun is not always correct; number, meaning and discourse must fit.

column2: However oldingi kutishga zid keyingi fikrni kiritadi. “Cheap, however unreliable”da narx yaxshi, ishonchlilik yomon. Savol qaysi jihatni so‘rayotganini tekshiring va faqat burilishdan oldingi ijobiy so‘zga yopishib qolmang.
column3: However introduces a contrast with the preceding expectation. Cheap but unreliable gives a positive price and negative reliability. Check which dimension the question asks about rather than stopping at an earlier positive word.

column2: Ikki narsa birga o‘zgargani biri boshqasiga sabab bo‘lganini isbotlamaydi. Matnda “associated with”mi yoki sababni tekshirgan tajribami, qarang. Uchinchi omil yoki teskari yo‘nalish ehtimoli bor; matndagi ehtiyotkor da’voni kuchaytirmang.
column3: Two variables changing together does not establish causation. Distinguish associated with from evidence designed to test a cause. A third factor or reverse direction may explain the link; preserve the passage’s level of certainty.

column2: “May”, “hypothesised”, “suggested” taxminni; “results showed” tadqiqot natijasini ko‘rsatishi mumkin. Ammo bitta signal so‘zning o‘zi yetmaydi: kim aytgani, metod va cheklovni o‘qing. Natija ham har qanday sharoitda universal isbot degani emas.
column3: May, hypothesised and suggested can mark a hypothesis; results showed can report findings. Read the speaker, method and limitations rather than relying on one word. A finding is not automatically universal proof.

column2: Bitta misol umumiy qoida uchun yetmasligi mumkin. “One school succeeded”dan “all schools succeed” chiqmaydi. Muallif misoldan qaysi chegaralangan fikrni ko‘rsatganini aniqlang; savoldagi guruh va chastota misoldan kengroqmi, tekshiring.
column3: One example may illustrate a point without proving a general rule. One school succeeded does not establish all schools succeed. Check whether the question broadens the group or frequency beyond the passage.

column2: Vaqtni alohida ustunlarga ajrating: avval A>B, keyin A<B bo‘lishi mumkin. Savoldagi yil va “initially/later”ni belgilang. Hozirgi holatni oldingi davrga ko‘chirmang; kesishish yoki o‘zgarish qaysi vaqtda bo‘lganini tekshiring.
column3: Separate time periods: A may exceed B initially and fall below B later. Match the question’s date and qualifiers to the relevant period. Do not project a later relationship backwards.

column2: Headingdagi possible ehtimolni, only yagona cheklovni bildiradi. Paragraf bir nechta sabab bersa “only cause” mos kelmaydi. Har headingning asosiy fikri bilan birga cheklovini ham tekshiring; mavzu bir xil bo‘lishining o‘zi yetmaydi.
column3: Possible expresses uncertainty; only excludes alternatives. A paragraph listing several causes cannot be summarised as the only cause. Check a heading’s qualifier as well as its subject.

column2: Har fikr yoniga kimning ovozi ekanini yozing: muallif, tadqiqotchi yoki iqtibosdagi odam. Muallif boshqaning fikrini xolis keltirishi yoki rad etishi mumkin. Iqtibos borligi muallif shu qarashga qo‘shilganini bildirmaydi.
column3: Label each view with its source: writer, researcher or quoted person. The writer may report a view neutrally or reject it. Quotation alone does not establish the writer’s agreement.

column2: Taymer nolga tushsa, sahifadagi yakunlangan yoki topshirilgan holatni tekshiring. Nol ko‘rinishi natija serverda saqlandi degan dalil emas. Avval mavjud javoblarni saqlang, keyin result yoki xato xabarini tekshiring; tasdiqsiz yangi urinish boshlamang.
column3: When the timer reaches zero, check the page’s submitted/completed status. Zero alone does not prove the server saved a result. Preserve answers and inspect the result or error before starting a replacement attempt.

column2: Article ro‘yxatidan o‘sha matnni ochib, mavjud davom ettirish holatini tanlang. Restart yoki yangi urinishni bosishdan oldin oldingi javoblar va timer holatini tekshiring. Davom ettirish tugmasi bo‘lmasa, urinish nomi va ko‘rinadigan statusni yuboring; men sessiya tiklandi deb taxmin qilmayman.
column3: Open the same article and use its available resume state. Before selecting Restart or a new attempt, check the saved responses and timer. If no resume control appears, share the item and visible status; I cannot assume an attempt was restored.

column2: 10/12 kabi hisoblagich qaysi sarlavha yonida turganini tekshiring: u belgilangan so‘zlar yoki bajarilgan lug‘at vazifalari sonini bildirishi mumkin. Uni avtomatik 10 ta so‘z yodlandi deb talqin qilmang. Label yoki ekran ko‘rinishini bersangiz, aniq maydonni tushuntiraman.
column3: Read the counter’s label: 10/12 may describe selected vocabulary or completed vocabulary steps. It does not by itself prove ten mastered words. Share the adjacent label or screenshot so I can identify the exact counter.

column2: Matndagi belgilangan so‘zni bosing yoki tanlang; lug‘at oynasi ochilsa kontekstga mos ma’no va so‘z turkumini tekshiring. Ochilmasa boshqa so‘zda sinang va tanlash rejimini tekshiring. Har qanday tagi chizilgan matn lug‘at tugmasi bo‘lishi shart emas.
column3: Tap or select the highlighted word and, if a dictionary panel opens, check the sense and part of speech for that sentence. If nothing opens, test another word and check selection mode. Not every underlined fragment is a dictionary control.

column2: Belgilangan so‘zlar ro‘yxatini ko‘rib, mavjud Save/Add boshqaruvida maqsad papkani tanlang. Har so‘zning to‘g‘ri ma’nosi tanlanganini tekshiring; keyin papkada saqlanganini tasdiqlang. Barchasini saqlash tugmasi ko‘rinmasa uni mavjud deb va’da qilmayman.
column3: Review the marked-word list and choose the destination folder in the available Save/Add control. Check each selected sense and verify the folder afterwards. I cannot promise a bulk-save control if none is shown.

column2: Saqlash oynasida yangi papka ochish o‘rniga mavjud folderni tanlang, so‘ng saqlangan ro‘yxatni tekshiring. Bir xil yozilgan so‘zning boshqa ma’nosi alohida yozuv bo‘lishi mumkin. Nusxalarni o‘chirishdan oldin sense va so‘z turkumini solishtiring.
column3: Choose an existing folder in the save dialog and verify its contents afterwards. Identical spelling with a different sense may be a distinct item. Compare sense and part of speech before deleting apparent duplicates.

column2: B2/C1 yorlig‘i matnning belgilangan qiyinlik darajasidir; sizning umumiy darajangiz yoki rasmiy sertifikatingiz emas. Murakkablik lug‘at, gap tuzilishi va fikrning yashirinligiga bog‘liq bo‘lishi mumkin. Mos darajani mustaqil tushunish va xato tahlili bilan tanlang.
column3: B2/C1 labels describe assigned text difficulty, not your certified overall level. Vocabulary, syntax and implicit meaning can affect difficulty. Choose using your independent comprehension and error review, not the label alone.

column2: Bir xil matnning urinish sanasi, aniqlik va sarflangan vaqtini solishtiring. Ikkinchi safar javobni eslab qolgan bo‘lishingiz mumkin; yaxshilanishni yangi matnda ham tekshiring. Oldingi urinish ko‘rinmasa, birinchi natijani o‘ylab topib solishtirmayman.
column3: Compare attempt dates, accuracy and time for the same article. A second attempt may benefit from remembering answers, so check transfer to a fresh text. If an earlier attempt is unavailable, I cannot invent a comparison.

column2: Matnni qayta ochishdan oldin asosiy g‘oya, 2–3 dalil va ularning bog‘lanishini xotiradan ayting. Bilmagan joyga belgi qo‘ying, keyin ruxsat etilgan reviewda matn bilan solishtiring. Faol recall vaqtida matndan tayyor javob izlash eslab qolishni tekshirmaydi.
column3: Before reopening, recall the main idea, two or three supporting details and their relationships. Mark gaps, then compare during the permitted review. Looking up answers during active recall defeats the memory task.

column2: Xotiradan aytgan fikringizni asl gap bilan solishtiring: qaysi raqam, sabab yoki ketma-ketlik o‘zgargan? To‘g‘ri shaklni o‘z so‘zingiz bilan qayta ayting, biroz tanaffusdan keyin yana eslang. Xatoni faqat o‘qib chiqish bilan cheklamang.
column3: Compare your recall with the original: which number, cause or sequence changed? Restate the corrected idea in your own words and retrieve it again after a delay. Merely rereading the correction is less informative than another recall attempt.

column2: Eng katta umumiy o‘zgarish va asosiy guruhlar orasidagi farqni tanlang. Overview barcha raqamlar ro‘yxati emas. Masalan, “Overall, car use rose, while bus use declined.” Ikkinchi fikr eng yuqori/past toifa yoki istisno bo‘lishi mumkin; grafikni ko‘rmasdan fakt qo‘shmayman.
column3: Choose the main overall change and a major comparison. An overview is not a list of figures. For example: Overall, car use rose, while bus use declined. A second feature might be the highest category or an exception; it must come from the actual chart.

column2: Ko‘tarilish yoki pasayish bo‘lmasa ham asosiy xususiyat bor: barqarorlik, tebranish, eng katta guruh yoki guruhlar farqi. “Overall, the figures fluctuated within a narrow range.” kabi gapni faqat grafik mos kelsa ishlating; yo‘q trendni yaratmang.
column3: Look for stability, fluctuation, the dominant category or a major comparison rather than inventing growth. “Overall, the figures fluctuated within a narrow range” works only when the chart supports it.

column2: 20%dan 30%ga — 10 percentage points o‘sish. Nisbiy o‘sish esa (30−20)/20×100 = 50%. “10 percent” bilan “10 percentage points”ni almashtirmang. Avval boshlang‘ich qiymat va o‘lchov birligini yozing, keyin farqni hisoblang.
column3: From 20% to 30% is an increase of 10 percentage points. The relative increase is (30−20)/20×100 = 50%. Keep the starting value and unit visible so percent and percentage points do not get confused.

column2: To yakuniy qiymatni, by o‘zgarish miqdorini beradi. “Sales rose to 80” — oxiri 80. “Sales rose by 20” — 20 qo‘shildi. “Sales rose from 60 to 80” — boshlanish va yakun. Yillar uchun “from 2000 to 2010” yoziladi.
column3: To introduces the final value; by introduces the amount of change. Sales rose to 80. Sales rose by 20. Sales rose from 60 to 80. Use from 2000 to 2010 for the time span.

column2: Vaqt ko‘rsatilmagan diagrammada umumiy taqqoslash uchun present simple odatda mos: “Group A has the largest share.” Agar sarlavha yoki matnda o‘tgan yil berilsa, past simple kerak bo‘lishi mumkin. Faqat x o‘qiga emas, barcha vaqt ma’lumotiga qarang.
column3: For a timeless comparison, present simple is often appropriate: Group A has the largest share. A past date in the title or caption may instead require past simple. Check every time reference, not just the axis.

column2: Turli birliklarni bevosita tenglashtirmang: tonna va foiz alohida o‘lchov. Har bir grafikning birligi bilan trendini tushuntiring; bog‘lanish bo‘lsa ehtiyotkor taqqoslang. Foizni miqdorga aylantirish uchun umumiy son kerak; berilmasa uni taxmin qilmang.
column3: Do not directly equate different units such as tonnes and percentages. Describe each chart using its own units and compare supported patterns. Converting a percentage to an amount requires a known total; do not invent one.

column2: O‘zgarmagan joyni aniq nomlang: “The bridge remained in the same location.” O‘zgarish bilan taqqoslang: “The road was widened, but the park was unchanged.” Uchinchisi: “The school retained its original position.” Xarita ko‘rsatmagan sababni qo‘shmang.
column3: Name unchanged features explicitly: The bridge remained in the same location. The road was widened, but the park was unchanged. The school retained its original position. Do not add a reason absent from the map.

column2: Siklik jarayonda sun’iy boshlanish yoki tugash yaratmang. Overviewda aylanish va asosiy bosqichlarni ayting: “Overall, the process is cyclical, with water returning to its initial state.” Tafsilotda tushuntirish uchun qulay bosqichdan boshlab doirani to‘liq kuzating.
column3: State that the process is cyclical and identify its main phases. Choose a convenient stage for explaining the details without claiming it is the only beginning. Follow the complete cycle and its return to an earlier state.

column2: Ishni bajaruvchi muhim yoki noma’lum bo‘lsa passive foydali: “The beans are dried.” Tabiiy jarayonda active mos: “Water evaporates.” Uchinchi misol: “The mixture is heated.” Jarayon va zamonga qarab shaklni tanlang; har gapni passive qilish shart emas.
column3: Use passive when the operation matters more than an unknown or unimportant agent: The beans are dried. Natural processes often use active: Water evaporates. The mixture is heated is another passive example; not every process sentence needs passive voice.

column2: Avval ikkala qiymatni bir birlikka o‘tkazing: 1 million = 1,000 thousand. 2.5 million va 900 thousandni 2.5 bilan 900 deb taqqoslamang; 2,500,000 va 900,000 deb tekshiring. Yakuniy gapda birlikni aniq yozing.
column3: Convert to a shared unit first: one million equals one thousand thousand. Compare 2.5 million with 900 thousand as 2,500,000 versus 900,000, not 2.5 versus 900. State the unit clearly in the final sentence.

column2: Raqamlarni o‘xshash trend yoki kattalik bo‘yicha guruhlang. Har paragrafda bir taqqoslashni ochib, unga 2–3 muhim qiymatni dalil qiling. Barcha nuqtani sanash o‘rniga eng katta, eng kichik va muhim o‘zgarishni tanlang.
column3: Group figures by shared trend or magnitude. Develop a comparison in each paragraph and support it with a few important values. Select meaningful extremes and changes rather than listing every data point.

column2: “To what extent” — qay darajada rozi yoki qarshi ekaningizni aniq ko‘rsating va shu pozitsiyani asoslang. To‘liq yoki qisman rozi bo‘lish mumkin, lekin sabablar pozitsiyaga mos bo‘lsin. Kirishdagi fikr bilan xulosa bir yo‘nalishda qolishi kerak.
column3: State how far you agree or disagree and justify that position. Full or qualified agreement is possible, but your reasons must support it. Keep the introduction, body and conclusion consistent.

column2: Savolning uch vazifasini ajrating: birinchi qarash, ikkinchi qarash va o‘z fikringiz. Har qarashni adolatli sabab bilan tushuntiring, keyin qaysi tomon nega kuchliroq ekanini belgilang. Fikrni faqat oxirgi bir gapga yashirib qo‘ymang.
column3: Identify all three duties: explain one view, explain the other, and give your opinion. Develop each fairly and show why your judgement follows. Do not leave your stance as an unsupported final sentence.

column2: Cause — muammoni paydo qilgan omil; problem — uning zararli holati yoki oqibati; solution — sabab yoki zararni kamaytiradigan choradir. Masalan, kam transport — sabab, tirbandlik — muammo, jamoat transportini yaxshilash — yechim. Aynan savol so‘ragan ikki qismga javob bering.
column3: A cause produces the issue; a problem is the harmful condition or consequence; a solution addresses it. Limited transport can be a cause, congestion the problem, and improved public transport a response. Answer the categories actually requested.

column2: “Outweigh” afzallik va kamchilikni sanashdan ko‘ra ularning ahamiyatini solishtirishni talab qiladi. Qaysi tomon kuchliroq va nima uchunligini yozing: ta’sir hajmi, davomiylik yoki kimga ta’sir qiladi. Uchta mayda foyda bitta katta zarardan avtomatik ustun emas.
column3: Outweigh requires a judgement about importance, not just a count of advantages and disadvantages. Compare scale, duration or who is affected. Three minor benefits do not automatically outweigh one substantial harm.

column2: Savoldagi ikkita so‘roq yoki buyruqni alohida yozing. Har biriga tezis va dalil rejalang; biri “why”, ikkinchisi “what can be done” bo‘lsa, ikkinchisiga yana sabab yozmang. Yakunda ikkala savolga aniq javob berilganini tekshiring.
column3: Write out both tasks separately and plan a direct answer and support for each. If one asks why and the other asks what can be done, do not answer both with causes. Check that neither task was omitted.

column2: Misoldan keyin “Bu qaysi sababni qanday ko‘rsatadi?” deb bir gap yozing. Bog‘lanishni tushuntira olmasangiz misol mavzudan chetda bo‘lishi mumkin. Topic sentence ta’lim xarajati haqida bo‘lsa, umumiy texnologiya qulayligi bunga o‘zi dalil emas.
column3: After the example, explain exactly how it supports the paragraph’s claim. If that connection is missing, the example may be irrelevant. A general convenience of technology does not by itself support a claim about education costs.

column2: Aniq foiz, tadqiqot yoki tashkilot nomini o‘ylab topmang. Fikringizni mantiqiy sabab va aniq, tasavvuriy deb tushunarli vaziyat bilan rivojlantiring. “For example, a student with a part-time job may…” kabi misol tekshirilmagan “87% of students”dan yaxshiroq.
column3: Do not fabricate precise statistics, studies or organisations. Develop a logical explanation and a clearly illustrative situation. “For example, a student with a part-time job may…” is preferable to an invented claim about 87% of students.

column2: Concession qarshi tomonning cheklangan kuchli jihatini tan oladi, tezisingizni bekor qilmaydi. “Although buses require investment, their long-term benefits justify the cost.” Keyin nega asosiy pozitsiya saqlanishini tushuntiring; butun qarama-qarshi fikrni tasdiqlab yubormang.
column3: A concession recognises a limited opposing point while retaining your thesis: Although buses require investment, their long-term benefits justify the cost. Explain why the main judgement still stands rather than endorsing the entire opposite position.

column2: This bir nechta oldingi fikrga ishora qilsa noaniq bo‘ladi. Aniqlashtiruvchi ot qo‘shing: “this increase”, “this policy”, “this delay”. So‘ng aynan qaysi hodisani nazarda tutganingizni tekshiring; faqat so‘zni almashtirish mantiqiy bog‘lanishni tuzatmasligi mumkin.
column3: This becomes unclear when several preceding ideas could be its reference. Add a precise noun: this increase, this policy, this delay. Check the intended referent; replacing a pronoun alone may not repair the logic.

column2: Connectorni gaplar orasidagi haqiqiy munosabatga qarab tanlang. Moreover qo‘shimcha, therefore natijani bildiradi. Har gap boshiga bog‘lovchi qo‘shish o‘rniga olmosh, sinonim va mavzu davomiyligidan foydalaning. Sabab bo‘lmasa therefore yozmang.
column3: Choose a connector for the actual relationship: moreover adds information; therefore marks a result. Use clear reference and topic continuity instead of attaching a connector to every sentence. Do not signal a consequence without a cause.

column2: Keng fikrni kim, qaysi sharoit va qanday mexanizm bilan toraytiring. “Technology is good” o‘rniga “Recorded lessons help working students review missed explanations.” Keyin nima uchun va qaysi cheklovda foyda berishini tushuntiring.
column3: Specify who benefits, under what conditions and through what mechanism. Replace Technology is good with Recorded lessons help working students review missed explanations. Then explain the benefit and its limits.

column2: Bir paragrafda bitta markaziy fikr bo‘lsin; unga xizmat qiladigan yaqin sabablar bo‘lishi mumkin. Har sababni tushuntirmay ro‘yxat qilishdan saqlaning. Agar ikkinchi sabab boshqa tezisga o‘tib ketsa, alohida paragraf oching.
column3: Use one central point per paragraph, with closely related reasons if they support it. Develop the reasoning instead of listing undeveloped ideas. Start another paragraph when a new reason changes the main focus.

column2: Xulosada kirishdagi pozitsiyani aniqroq, qisqa qaytaring va asosiy sababni jamlang. Yangi qarama-qarshi fikr yoki yangi dalil kiritmang. “May be good or bad” kabi noaniq yakun aniq tezisni zaiflashtirishi mumkin.
column3: Restate the same judgement concisely and synthesise its main support. Avoid a new argument or opposing stance. An uncertain ending such as may be good or bad can weaken an otherwise clear thesis.

column2: Gap uzunligini so‘z soni emas, uni xatosiz boshqarishingiz belgilaydi. Har bir fe’lning egasi, bog‘lovchi va olmosh ishorasini tekshiring. Ikki mustaqil fikr faqat vergul bilan ulangan bo‘lsa, nuqta yoki mos bog‘lovchi qo‘ying. Aniqlik murakkablikdan ustun.
column3: Judge a sentence by control, not length alone. Check subjects, verb agreement, connectors and references. If two independent clauses are joined only by a comma, use proper punctuation or a conjunction. Prioritise clarity over complexity.

column2: Speak or Die’dagi qisqa previewda mavzuni o‘qing va uch tayanchni tanlang: javob, sabab, misol. Bu vaqtni to‘liq matn yodlashga sarflamang. Taymer va recording holatini ekrandan tekshiring; preview tugashi bilan gapirishga tayyor bo‘ling.
column3: During the short Speak or Die preview, identify three cues: answer, reason and example. Do not try to memorise a script. Check the displayed timer and recording state, then be ready to speak.

column2: 60 soniyani tayyor skriptsiz to‘ldirish uchun javob → sabab → aniq voqea → qisqa xulosa tartibini ishlating. 3–4 kalit so‘z yetarli. Bir fikrni qayta aytish o‘rniga qachon, kim bilan va nega degan tafsilot qo‘shing.
column3: Use answer, reason, specific experience and brief conclusion. Prepare a few cues rather than a script. Extend with when, who and why instead of repeating the same sentence until sixty seconds pass.

column2: Javob erta tugasa, mazmunli misol yoki taqqoslash qo‘shing: qachon bo‘ldi, natijasi nima, hozir nimasi boshqacha? Savoldan chetga chiqib sun’iy gapni cho‘zmang. Keyingi urinishda uch tayanchli reja bilan vaqtni mashq qiling.
column3: Add a relevant example, comparison or consequence if you finish early. Explain when it happened, what resulted or what changed. Do not pad with unrelated talk; practise timing with a three-cue plan next time.

column2: Kutilmagan mavzuda mukammal g‘oya izlamang. Savol turini taning, oddiy haqiqiy misol tanlang, sabab va tafsilot bilan kengaytiring. Bilmagan faktni uydirmang; shaxsiy tajriba yoki ehtiyotkor umumiy misol bilan javob bering.
column3: Identify the question type, choose a simple familiar example and expand with a reason and detail. Do not invent facts to sound impressive. Use your experience or a clearly hypothetical illustration.

column2: So‘zni unutib qolsangiz, vazifasi yoki ko‘rinishini ayting: “It’s a tool for opening bottles.” Yoki sodda sinonim ishlating va davom eting. Uzoq sukutdan ko‘ra qisqa qayta ifodalash foydali; aniq nomni keyingi tahlilda lug‘atdan tekshiring.
column3: Describe the function or appearance: It’s a tool for opening bottles. Use a simpler synonym and continue. A short paraphrase is more useful than a long silence; look up the exact word during review.

column2: Brauzerning mikrofon ruxsati bilan sahifadagi yozuv indikatori alohida narsalar. Ruxsatni tekshiring, so‘ng recording holati va ovoz belgisi o‘zgarayotganini ko‘ring. RIWI dictation faqat qurilmada matnga aylantiradi; Speaking yozuvi esa boshqa modulning jarayoni.
column3: Browser microphone permission and an active recording are separate. Check permission, then the page’s recording indicator. RIWI dictation produces editable text on-device; a Speaking recording follows that module’s separate workflow.

column2: Savol qaytarilsa, recording/submission qabul qilinganmi va keyingi bosqichga o‘tilganmi, tekshiring. Bir xil savolni yangi bosqich deb taxmin qilmang. Sahifa nomi, savol va ko‘rinadigan status bilan xabar bering; takror bosishdan oldin javobni saqlang.
column3: Check whether your response was accepted and the next stage actually started. A repeated question is not proof of progress. Report the page, question and visible status, preserving your response before repeated retries.

column2: Yozuv tugashi, serverga topshirish va feedback tayyor bo‘lishi uch alohida holat. Avval audio preview, keyin submitted status, keyin baholash/xato xabarini tekshiring. Qayta yuborishdan oldin mavjud yozuvni saqlang; ko‘rinmagan bahoni tayyor deb aytmayman.
column3: Recording completion, submission and feedback availability are distinct. Check the audio preview, submitted status and any grading/error message in that order. Preserve the recording before retrying; absent feedback cannot be treated as a completed score.

column2: Playbackda ovoz yo‘q yoki qurilma ruxsati rad etilgan bo‘lsa capture muammosini tekshiring. Audio eshitilib, submitted bo‘lsa-yu feedback chiqmasa, topshirish/baholash holatini tekshiring. Ikkalasini bir xato deb olmang; ko‘rinadigan xabar sababni toraytiradi.
column3: Silent playback or denied permission suggests a capture problem. Audible, submitted audio without feedback requires checking submission or grading state. These are different failure points; the visible error helps distinguish them.

column2: Yozuvni bir marta mazmun, ikkinchi marta takroriy filler uchun tinglang. “Um”, “like”, “you know” ishlatilgan joylarni qisqa qayd qiling; hammasini taqiqlash shart emas. Keraksiz takror o‘rniga qisqa tabiiy pauza bilan shu javobni yana ayting.
column3: Listen once for meaning and again for repeated fillers. Note unnecessary um, like or you know, rather than banning every natural discourse marker. Repeat the answer using brief pauses where habitual filler adds nothing.

column2: Partner sahifasidagi mavjudlik holati joriy ulanish va presence yangilanishiga bog‘liq bo‘lishi mumkin. Oddiy profil ochiqligi faol call kutayotganingizni isbotlamaydi. Find Partner sahifasini ochib holatni tekshiring; boshqalarning ko‘rinishini doimiy onlayn dalil deb olmang.
column3: Partner availability may depend on the page’s current connection and presence updates. Having a profile does not prove you are waiting for a call. Check Find Partner and its status; an old online indicator is not permanent evidence.

column2: Qidiruvdagi level filter faqat ko‘rinadigan nomzodlarni saralaydi; profil darajasini tahrirlash boshqa amal. Filtrni o‘zgartirib ro‘yxatni tekshiring, profilga o‘zgartirish kiritilgan deb hisoblamang. O‘zingizga mos suhbatdoshni mashq maqsadi bilan tanlang.
column3: A search-level filter changes the candidate list; editing your profile level is a separate action. Change the filter and inspect the results without assuming your profile changed. Choose a partner suited to your practice goal.

column2: Male/Female/Everyone qidiruv ro‘yxatini tanlangan mezon bo‘yicha filtrlashga xizmat qiladi. Bu foydalanuvchining huquqi yoki til darajasini o‘zgartirmaydi. Natija bo‘lmasa Everyone bilan tekshirish mumkin; ko‘rinmagan odamning shaxsiy ma’lumotini taxmin qilmang.
column3: Male, Female and Everyone filter the partner list. They do not change account permissions or language level. If no matches appear, try Everyone; do not infer private facts about users who are not shown.

column2: Taklif yuborgach, qabul qilingan yoki rad etilgan holatni kuting; yuborildi degani call boshlandi emas. Qabul qilinsa mikrofon va ulanish holatini tekshiring. Bir odamga ketma-ket takliflar yuborish o‘rniga ko‘rinadigan holatga qarang.
column3: Wait for an accepted or declined invitation state. Sent does not mean the call has started. After acceptance, check the microphone and connection; avoid repeatedly inviting the same person while an invitation is pending.

column2: Kiruvchi taklifdagi Decline/Rad etish faqat shu taklifni rad etadi; Block alohida cheklovdir. Shunchaki hozir gaplasha olmasangiz Decline’ni tanlang. Tugma nomini o‘qing, tasdiqlash bo‘lsa qaysi amal so‘ralganini tekshiring.
column3: Decline rejects the current invitation; Block is a separate restriction. Use Decline if you simply cannot talk now. Read the control and any confirmation so you do not unintentionally choose a stronger action.

column2: Avval tarmoq, qurilma ruxsati va sahifadagi call holatini tekshiring. Qayta qo‘ng‘iroq qilishdan oldin eski call tugaganini tasdiqlang. Muammo takrorlansa vaqt, qurilma va xato xabarini Supportga bering; boshqaning aloqa ma’lumotini chatga kiritmang.
column3: Check network, device permission and the call state. Confirm that the old call ended before starting another. If disconnections recur, report the time, device and error without sharing the partner’s private contact details.

column2: Partner bergan IELTS-style baho tengdosh fikridir; rasmiy imtihonchi bahosi yoki sertifikat emas. Uni fluency, vocabulary, grammar va pronunciation bo‘yicha amaliy maslahat sifatida ko‘ring. Bitta call natijasidan umumiy bandni kafolatlab bo‘lmaydi.
column3: A partner’s IELTS-style rating is peer feedback, not an official examiner score or certificate. Use it as practice feedback on fluency, vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation. One call cannot guarantee your overall band.

column2: Rating oynasi callning yakunlangan holati va modulning shartlariga bog‘liq. Oyna chiqmasa, call tugaganmi va sahifada review amali bormi, tekshiring. Men ko‘rinmagan oynani ochildi deb aytmayman; aniq call holatini yozing.
column3: The rating prompt depends on the call reaching the appropriate ended state and the module’s conditions. If it is absent, check whether the call ended and a review control is available. Share the visible state rather than assuming a prompt appeared.

column2: Bitta rating — bir suhbat haqidagi fikr; average — bir nechta ruxsatli ratingning yig‘ma ko‘rsatkichi. O‘rtachani tushunishda nechta baho va qaysi mezon ekanini tekshiring. Kichik namuna yoki yumaloqlash bir call bilan farq chiqarishi mumkin.
column3: One rating concerns one call; an average aggregates available ratings. Check the number of ratings and the criterion. A small sample or rounding may explain why the average differs from one recent call.

column2: Nomaqbul muomalani Report/Support orqali aniq vaqt va hodisa tavsifi bilan bildiring. Zarur bo‘lsa callni tugating va mavjud Block amalidan foydalaning. Shaxsiy ma’lumotni ommaviy tarqatmang; RIWI chatga shikoyat yozishning o‘zi report yuborilganini anglatmaydi.
column3: Use Report or Support with the time and a factual description. End the call and use the available Block control if needed. Avoid publicly sharing private details; describing it to RIWI alone does not submit a formal report.

column2: Used to + asosiy fe’l — avvalgi odat yoki holat. Be used to + ot/-ing — ko‘nikkanlik. Get used to — ko‘nikib borish. Uch misol: “I used to cycle.” — Avval velosiped minardim. “I am used to cycling.” — Bunga ko‘nikkanman. “I’m getting used to cycling.” — Ko‘nikib boryapman.
column3: Used to + base verb describes a past habit/state. Be used to + noun/-ing means accustomed to; get used to means become accustomed. Examples: I used to cycle. I am used to cycling. I’m getting used to cycling.

column2: Hardly gap boshida vaqt ma’nosida kelsa yordamchi fe’l egadan oldinga chiqadi: Hardly had + ega + V3 + when. “Hardly had I arrived when it rained.” “Hardly had she sat down when the phone rang.” “I had hardly arrived when it rained.” Oxirgisida hardly boshda emas, inversion yo‘q.
column3: Fronted temporal hardly triggers auxiliary–subject inversion, commonly Hardly had + subject + past participle + when. Examples: Hardly had I arrived when it rained. Hardly had she sat down when the phone rang. I had hardly arrived when it rained has no fronted inversion.

column2: If only — kuchli istak yoki afsus; only if — qat’iy shart. “If only I knew!” — Qani bilsam! “You can leave only if you finish.” — Faqat tugatsangiz ketasiz. “Only if you finish can you leave.” — Shart boshga chiqsa bosh gapda inversion bo‘ladi.
column3: If only expresses a strong wish/regret; only if sets a condition. Examples: If only I knew! You can leave only if you finish. Only if you finish can you leave. Fronting only if causes inversion in the main clause, not inside the if-clause.

column2: Hozirgi afsus uchun wish + past form, o‘tmishdagi afsus uchun wish + had + V3. “I wish I knew.” — Hozir bilmayman. “I wish I had studied.” — O‘shanda o‘qimaganimdan afsusdaman. “I wish I could swim.” — Suzishni bilsam edi. Past form bu yerda doim o‘tgan vaqt degani emas.
column3: Use wish + past form for an unreal present and wish + past perfect for past regret. Examples: I wish I knew. I wish I had studied. I wish I could swim. The past form in the first example marks remoteness rather than past time.

column2: Would ratherdan keyin boshqa ega kelsa hozirgi/kelajak istagi past form bilan beriladi. Bir xil egada base verb ishlatiladi. “I’d rather you went now.” — Siz hozir ketsangiz ma’qul. “I’d rather stay.” — Qolganim ma’qul. “I’d rather you had called.” — O‘shanda qo‘ng‘iroq qilganingiz ma’qul edi.
column3: With a different subject, would rather uses a past form for a present/future preference. With the same subject, use the base verb. Examples: I’d rather you went now. I’d rather stay. I’d rather you had called expresses a past preference/regret.

column2: Have + narsa + V3 ishni boshqasiga bajartirishni bildiradi; zamon have orqali o‘zgaradi. “I had my hair cut.” — Sochimni oldirdim. “She is having her car repaired.” — Mashinasini tuzattiryapti. “We’ll have the windows cleaned.” — Derazalarni tozalattiramiz. Kontekstda boshdan kechirilgan hodisani ham bildirishi mumkin.
column3: Have + object + past participle often means arranging for someone to do something. Tense is carried by have. Examples: I had my hair cut. She is having her car repaired. We’ll have the windows cleaned. Context can also give an experience/affected-person meaning.

column2: Make + object + base verb majburlash/sabab bo‘lish; get + object + to-infinitive ko‘ndirish/tashkil etish bo‘lishi mumkin. “They made me wait.” — Kuttirishdi. “I got him to help.” — Yordamga ko‘ndirdim. “I was made to wait.” — Passive make’da to qaytadi.
column3: Make takes object + base verb; get takes object + to-infinitive, often with persuasion/arrangement. Examples: They made me wait. I got him to help. I was made to wait. Passive make restores to.

column2: Aniqlanayotgan ot ishtirokchi bo‘lsa active -ing yoki passive V3 qisqartirish mumkin. “Students who live here” → “Students living here”. “Books that were written in 2000” → “Books written in 2000”. “The man who called”ni har qanday zamonda “the man calling” qilish mumkin emas: vaqt va ma’no saqlanishi kerak.
column3: A relative clause may reduce to an active -ing or passive participle when the meaning fits. Examples: students who live here → students living here; books that were written in 2000 → books written in 2000. The man who called cannot always become the man calling without changing time/meaning.

column2: Kirishdagi participle harakati bosh gap egasiga tegishli bo‘lsin. “Walking home, I saw a dog.” — Men yurdim. “While I was walking home, it started raining.” — Yomg‘ir yurgani yo‘q. “Having finished the work, she left.” — U tugatdi va ketdi. Ega mos bo‘lmasa to‘liq clause yozing.
column3: The understood subject of an introductory participle normally matches the main-clause subject. Examples: Walking home, I saw a dog. While I was walking home, it started raining. Having finished the work, she left. Use a full clause to avoid a dangling modifier.

column2: Having + V3 bir ish boshqasidan oldin tugaganini aniq ko‘rsatadi. “Having finished dinner, we left.” — Ovqat tugagach ketdik. “Finishing dinner, we discussed the trip.” — Tugatayotib gaplashdik. “Having been warned, he stayed away.” — Ogohlantirilgach yaqinlashmadi. -ingning o‘zi ham kontekstda oldingi ishni bildirishi mumkin.
column3: Having + past participle explicitly marks prior completion. Examples: Having finished dinner, we left. Finishing dinner, we discussed the trip. Having been warned, he stayed away. A simple -ing clause can also describe an earlier action when context makes the sequence clear.

column2: Not only gap boshida kelib clause’ni cheklasa yordamchi fe’l egadan oldinga chiqadi. “Not only did she study, but she also worked.” “Not only is it cheap, but it is also reliable.” “She not only studies but also works.” Oxirgisida inversion yo‘q.
column3: Fronted clause-level not only triggers inversion. Examples: Not only did she study, but she also worked. Not only is it cheap, but it is also reliable. She not only studies but also works does not require inversion.

column2: Neither…nor bilan ikki birlik ega odatda birlik fe’l oladi. Aralash sonli egada yaqin ega bilan moslik keng ishlatiladi; noqulay gapni qayta tuzing. “Neither Ali nor Vali is here.” “Neither the teacher nor the students are ready.” “Neither the students nor the teacher is ready.”
column3: Two singular subjects normally take a singular verb. With mixed number, agreement commonly follows the nearer subject; rephrase awkward cases. Examples: Neither Ali nor Vali is here. Neither the teacher nor the students are ready. Neither the students nor the teacher is ready.

column2: Few/a few sanaladigan ko‘plik otlar, little/a little sanalmaydigan otlar bilan. A bo‘lmasa yetarli emas degan salbiy ohang kuchliroq. “Few students came.” — Juda kam. “A few students came.” — Bir nechtasi. “We have a little time.” — Oz bo‘lsa-da vaqt bor.
column3: Few/a few modify plural count nouns; little/a little modify uncount nouns. Without a, the meaning is more negative. Examples: Few students came. A few students came. We have a little time. Compare insufficient quantity with some available quantity.

column2: Fewer sanaladigan ko‘plik, less odatda sanalmaydigan miqdor bilan. “Fewer cars arrived.” “We used less water.” “The trip took less than two hours.” Vaqt, pul va masofa kabi bitta o‘lchov deb qaralgan ifodalarda less ishlatilishi mumkin.
column3: Use fewer for plural count nouns and less for uncount quantity. Examples: Fewer cars arrived. We used less water. The trip took less than two hours. Less is also common for amounts of time, money and distance treated as a measure.

column2: Each alohida bittalab qaraydi; “of the students” ko‘plik bo‘lsa ham asosiy ega each. “Each of the students is ready.” “Each of us has a task.” “The students are ready.” Oxirgi gapda ega students, shuning uchun are.
column3: Each is the singular head; of the students does not turn it into a plural subject. Examples: Each of the students is ready. Each of us has a task. The students are ready has a plural head and takes are.

column2: None of bilan fe’l ma’no va otga bog‘liq. Sanalmaydigan ot bilan birlik: “None of the water is clean.” Ko‘plik ot bilan plural ham, rasmiyroq singular ham uchraydi: “None of the students are ready.” “None of the students is ready.” Kontekst va uslubni saqlang.
column3: Agreement depends on the noun and intended meaning. Examples: None of the water is clean. None of the students are ready. None of the students is ready. Plural agreement is common with plural count nouns; singular is also used, especially for a not-one interpretation.

column2: The number of — sonning o‘zi, birlik; a number of — bir qancha, ko‘plik. “The number of students is rising.” — Talabalar soni oshmoqda. “A number of students are absent.” — Bir nechtasi yo‘q. “The number has doubled.” — Son ikki baravar bo‘ldi.
column3: The number of has a singular head referring to a total; a number of means several and takes plural agreement. Examples: The number of students is rising. A number of students are absent. The number has doubled.

column2: As if + past form hozirgi vaziyatdan uzoq, go‘yoki haqiqiy emas degan ma’noni bera oladi. “He talks as if he knew everything.” “She looks as if she is tired.” “He acted as if he had seen a ghost.” Ikkinchisida holat haqiqatan bo‘lishi mumkin, uchinchisida oldingi hodisa.
column3: A past form after as if can mark an unreal present comparison. Examples: He talks as if he knew everything. She looks as if she is tired suggests a plausible current state. He acted as if he had seen a ghost refers to an earlier event.

column2: So + adjective/adverb + that; such + noun phrase + that. “It was so cold that we stayed in.” “It was such a cold day that we stayed in.” “She spoke so quietly that I couldn’t hear.” Such a/an faqat birlik sanaladigan ot birikmasida keladi.
column3: Use so + adjective/adverb + that, but such + noun phrase + that. Examples: It was so cold that we stayed in. It was such a cold day that we stayed in. She spoke so quietly that I couldn’t hear. Use a/an only with an appropriate singular count noun.

column2: Too — kerakdan ortiq, natijani to‘sishi mumkin; enough — yetarli. “It is too heavy to lift.” — Ko‘tarishga og‘irlik qiladi. “It is light enough to carry.” — Ko‘tarish uchun yetarlicha yengil. “We have enough time to finish.” Enough sifatdan keyin, otdan oldin.
column3: Too expresses excess; enough expresses sufficiency. Examples: It is too heavy to lift. It is light enough to carry. We have enough time to finish. Enough follows an adjective but precedes a noun.

column2: Unless ko‘pincha “except if / agar…bo‘lmasa” degani, lekin har bir if not gapini mexanik almashtirmang. “Unless it rains, we’ll walk.” “If it doesn’t rain, we’ll walk.” “I’ll be surprised if he doesn’t come.” Oxirgisini unless bilan almashtirish ma’noni o‘zgartiradi.
column3: Unless often means except if, but cannot mechanically replace every if not. Compare: Unless it rains, we’ll walk. If it doesn’t rain, we’ll walk. I’ll be surprised if he doesn’t come does not preserve its meaning with a simple unless substitution.

column2: Provided that va as long as shartni bildiradi: faqat shu shart bajarilsa. “You can borrow it provided that you return it.” “You may stay as long as you are quiet.” “I’ll help as long as I have time.” As long as boshqa kontekstda davomiylikni ham bildirishi mumkin.
column3: Provided that and conditional as long as introduce a condition. Examples: You can borrow it provided that you return it. You may stay as long as you are quiet. I’ll help as long as I have time. As long as can also express duration in another context.

column2: Third conditional passive shakllari: if + had been + V3; would have been + V3. “If it had been repaired, it would have worked.” “If we had left it outside, it would have been damaged.” “If it had been checked, the error would have been found.” O‘tgan real bo‘lmagan natijani ko‘rsatasiz.
column3: Use had been + past participle in a passive if-clause and would have been + past participle for a passive result. Examples: If it had been repaired, it would have worked. If we had left it outside, it would have been damaged. If it had been checked, the error would have been found.

column2: Must have + V3 — o‘tmish haqida kuchli xulosa; could have + V3 — mumkin bo‘lgan hodisa yoki ishlatilmagan imkoniyat. “She must have left.” “She could have taken a taxi.” “You could have called me.” Qaysi ma’no ekanini kontekst belgilaydi; could have doim sodir bo‘lmagan degani emas.
column3: Must have marks a strong past deduction; could have may express past possibility or an unused opportunity. Examples: She must have left. She could have taken a taxi. You could have called me. Could have does not always imply that the event did not happen.

column2: Needn’t have done — ish bajarilgan, ammo kerak bo‘lmagan. Didn’t need to do — zarurat bo‘lmagan; ish bajarilgan-bajarilmagani kontekstdan bilinadi. “You needn’t have bought bread.” “I didn’t need to work, so I rested.” “I didn’t need to cook, but I did.” Oxirgi gapni imkonsiz deb olmang.
column3: Needn’t have done means it happened but was unnecessary. Didn’t need to do states absence of necessity; context tells whether it happened. Examples: You needn’t have bought bread. I didn’t need to work, so I rested. I didn’t need to cook, but I did.

column2: Should have + V3 tanqid/afsus yoki kutishni bildiradi. “You should have called.” — Qo‘ng‘iroq qilishingiz kerak edi. “The train should have arrived by now.” — Hozirgacha kelgan bo‘lishi kerak. “I should have checked.” — Tekshirmaganimdan afsus. Qaysi ma’no ekanini vaziyatdan tanlang.
column3: Should have can express criticism/regret or expectation. Examples: You should have called. The train should have arrived by now. I should have checked. Context distinguishes an unmet obligation from an expected past event.

column2: Bilvosita savolda ichki clause darak tartibida: ega + fe’l. “Where is he?” → “Do you know where he is?” “What does she need?” → “Tell me what she needs.” “Is it open?” → “I wonder if it is open.” Ichki gapda savol uchun qo‘shilgan do/does qolmaydi.
column3: An embedded question uses statement order. Examples: Where is he? → Do you know where he is? What does she need? → Tell me what she needs. Is it open? → I wonder if it is open. Remove question-only do-support inside the embedded clause.

column2: Wh-savolda wh-so‘z, keyin ega + fe’l; yes/no savolda if/whether + ega + fe’l ishlating. “I know where she lives.” “Tell me whether you agree.” “What he said surprised me.” Uchinchi misolda butun wh-clause bosh gapning egasi.
column3: Use a wh-word followed by subject + verb, or if/whether for a yes/no question. Examples: I know where she lives. Tell me whether you agree. What he said surprised me. In the last example, the whole clause functions as the subject.

column2: Ba’zi fe’llar object + to-infinitive qolipini talab qiladi; bu fe’lning lug‘aviy xususiyati. “I want you to stay.” “She asked me to help.” “They told us to wait.” Har fe’lga shu qolipni qo‘llamang: make me wait’da to yo‘q. Lug‘atdan verb patternni tekshiring.
column3: Some verbs license object + to-infinitive as part of their lexical pattern. Examples: I want you to stay. She asked me to help. They told us to wait. Do not generalise to all verbs: make me wait has no to. Check the dictionary pattern.

column2: Prepositiondan keyin fe’l kerak bo‘lsa odatda -ing shakli keladi. “She is good at drawing.” “I left without speaking.” “I look forward to meeting you.” Oxirgisida to infinitive belgisi emas, preposition; shuning uchun meet emas meeting.
column3: When a verb follows a preposition, use the -ing form. Examples: She is good at drawing. I left without speaking. I look forward to meeting you. In the last sentence, to is a preposition rather than an infinitive marker.

column2: Stop doing — shu ishni to‘xtatish; stop to do — boshqa ishni biror maqsad uchun to‘xtatish. “He stopped smoking.” — Chekishni tashladi. “He stopped to smoke.” — Chekish uchun to‘xtadi. “We stopped walking to rest.” — Dam olish uchun yurishni to‘xtatdik.
column3: Stop doing means cease that activity; stop to do means pause another activity for a purpose. Examples: He stopped smoking. He stopped to smoke. We stopped walking to rest. The infinitive gives the purpose of stopping.

column2: Remember doing — o‘tgan hodisani eslash; remember to do — kerakli ishni unutmay bajarish. “I remember locking the door.” “Remember to lock the door.” “She remembered to call.” Oxirgisi u qo‘ng‘iroq qilishni unutmaganini bildiradi.
column3: Remember doing recalls an earlier event; remember to do means not forgetting a required action. Examples: I remember locking the door. Remember to lock the door. She remembered to call means she did not forget the action.

column2: Try doing — yechim sifatida sinash; try to do — bajarishga urinish. “Try restarting the phone.” — Qayta yoqishni sinang. “I tried to open the door.” — Ochishga urindim. “Try adding less salt.” — Tuzni kamaytirishni sinang. Urinish har doim muvaffaqiyatni bildirmaydi.
column3: Try doing tests a possible method; try to do attempts an action. Examples: Try restarting the phone. I tried to open the door. Try adding less salt. An attempt does not by itself establish success.

column2: Avoid fe’li ortidan boshqa fe’l kelsa -ing oladi: avoid doing. “Avoid making noise.” “She avoids driving at night.” “We avoided repeating the mistake.” To-infinitive bu qolipga mos emas; bu qoidani barcha fe’llarga ko‘chirmang.
column3: Avoid takes an -ing complement, not a to-infinitive. Examples: Avoid making noise. She avoids driving at night. We avoided repeating the mistake. This is the pattern for avoid, not a rule for every verb.

column2: Ko‘p fe’llardan keyin object clause’dagi that tushishi mumkin: “I think (that) it works.” Ammo subject clause boshida that odatda kerak: “That he left surprised me.” “She said (that) she was ready.” Tushirish gapni noaniq qilsa thatni saqlang.
column3: That is often optional in object complement clauses but normally retained in a clause used as subject. Examples: I think (that) it works. That he left surprised me. She said (that) she was ready. Retain that when omission creates ambiguity.

column2: Bank ma’nosini atrofidagi so‘zlardan tanlang: “deposit money at the bank” — moliyaviy tashkilot; “sit on the river bank” — qirg‘oq; “bank on your help” — yordamga tayanmoq. Lug‘atda birinchi tarjimani avtomatik olmang; butun gap va so‘z turkumini tekshiring.
column3: Choose the sense from context: deposit money at the bank means a financial institution; sit on the river bank refers to an edge of land; bank on your help means rely on it. Check the sentence and part of speech rather than taking the first translation.

column2: Record shakli o‘zgarmasa ham vazifasi o‘zgaradi. “Keep a record.” — Ot, /ˈrekɔːd/. “Record your voice.” — Fe’l, /rɪˈkɔːd/. “The record is accurate.” — Ot. Artikllar, ega-fe’l o‘rni va urg‘u ma’noni ajratishga yordam beradi.
column3: The same spelling can have different roles. Keep a record uses a noun, commonly /ˈrekɔːd/. Record your voice uses a verb, /rɪˈkɔːd/. The record is accurate uses the noun. Syntax and stress help distinguish them.

column2: British Englishda practice ot, practise fe’l; American Englishda practice ikkala vazifada. “Daily practice helps.” — Ot. “I practise daily.” — Britancha fe’l. “I practice daily.” — Amerikacha fe’l. Bir matnda tanlangan imlo uslubini izchil saqlang.
column3: In British English, practice is the noun and practise the verb; American English uses practice for both. Examples: Daily practice helps. I practise daily. I practice daily. Keep the chosen spelling convention consistent.

column2: Make a decision va do homework odatiy collocationlardir; make/do’ni har safar so‘zma-so‘z tarjima qilib tanlab bo‘lmaydi. Uch misol: “We made a decision.” “I do my homework.” “She made a mistake.” Lug‘atdan alohida so‘zni emas, birikmani saqlang.
column3: These are established collocations rather than a universal translation rule. Examples: We made a decision. I do my homework. She made a mistake. Learn and check the complete phrase instead of translating make or do in isolation.

column2: Birikma bilan yodlang: interested in, depend on. Uch misol: “I’m interested in music.” “She is interested in learning.” “It depends on the weather.” In’dan keyingi fe’l -ing oladi; depend’dan keyin on predlogini unutmang.
column3: Learn the complete patterns interested in and depend on. Examples: I’m interested in music. She is interested in learning. It depends on the weather. Use -ing after the preposition in when a verb follows it.

column2: Suggest odatda -ing yoki that-clause oladi. “I suggest going early.” “She suggested that we leave.” “He suggested a different route.” Oddiy taklif ma’nosida “suggest to go” ishlatmang; boshqa fe’lning infinitive qolipini bunga ko‘chirmang.
column3: Suggest commonly takes -ing, a that-clause or a noun phrase. Examples: I suggest going early. She suggested that we leave. He suggested a different route. Avoid transferring another verb’s to-infinitive pattern to suggest.

column2: Knowledge boshidagi k va debt ichidagi b talaffuz qilinmaydi. “Knowledge is useful.” “He paid the debt.” “I know the answer.” Lug‘atdagi IPAni ko‘rib, ovozni bo‘laklab tinglang; imlodagi har harfni ovozga aylantirmang.
column3: The k in knowledge and b in debt are silent. Examples: Knowledge is useful. He paid the debt. I know the answer. Use dictionary IPA and audio instead of pronouncing every written letter.

column2: /ɪ/ va /iː/ faqat uzunlik bilan emas, unli sifati bilan ham farq qiladi. Juftlar: ship–sheep, live–leave, sit–seat. Avval qaysi birini eshitganingizni tanlang, keyin yozib qayta tinglang. RIWI matnli savoldan talaffuzingizni eshitdim deb aytmaydi.
column3: The contrast involves vowel quality as well as length. Practise ship–sheep, live–leave and sit–seat. Identify the heard word before recording and comparing your version. A text-only question does not allow RIWI to judge your pronunciation.

column2: Advice va information odatda sanalmaydigan otlar: an yoki many bilan to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri ishlamaydi. “She gave me some advice.” “I need a piece of information.” “We received useful information.” Alohida birlik kerak bo‘lsa a piece of yoki mos sanaladigan ot tanlang.
column3: Advice and information are normally uncountable. Examples: She gave me some advice. I need a piece of information. We received useful information. Use a measure phrase or another appropriate count noun for an individual item.

column2: Prefiksni faqat birinchi harfga qarab yaratib bo‘lmaydi; tayyor so‘zni lug‘atdan tekshiring. Misollar: unhappy, impossible, irregular. In- ayrim tovushlar oldida im-/ir-/il- bo‘ladi, ammo har so‘z bunday prefiks olmaydi. Ma’no va amaldagi imlo ikkalasi kerak.
column3: Do not invent a negative prefix from the first letter alone; verify the established word. Examples: unhappy, impossible, irregular. In- has forms such as im-, ir- and il- in some words, but these patterns do not license every imagined word.

column2: Hope — ot/fe’l; hopeful — umidli; hopeless — umidsiz yoki juda yomon degan kontekstli sifat. “We still have hope.” “She is hopeful about the result.” “The situation seemed hopeless.” Qo‘shimcha ma’noni o‘zgartiradi; har -less so‘zi barcha kontekstda oddiy inkor emas.
column3: Hope is a noun/verb; hopeful and hopeless are adjectives with context-dependent meanings. Examples: We still have hope. She is hopeful about the result. The situation seemed hopeless. Learn the word family with its actual usage.

column2: Lug‘atdagi informal/slang labelini va birikmaning ohangini tekshiring. “Kids” o‘rniga “children”, “a lot of” o‘rniga vaziyatga qarab “many”, “stuff” o‘rniga aniq ot yozish mumkin. Murakkab sinonimni majburan qo‘shmang; ma’no va collocation saqlansin.
column3: Check dictionary register labels and the phrase’s tone. Depending on context, children may suit better than kids, and a precise noun better than stuff. Do not replace words with complex synonyms unless meaning and collocation remain accurate.

column2: Saqlashdan oldin lemma, so‘z turkumi va shu gapdagi ma’noni tekshiring. Bir ma’noni bir papkaga qayta qo‘shish bilan boshqa ma’noni saqlash boshqa narsalar. Bankning pul va qirg‘oq ma’nolarini shunchaki bir xil yozilgani uchun birlashtirmang.
column3: Check lemma, part of speech and contextual sense before saving. Re-saving the same sense differs from storing another sense. Do not merge financial bank and river bank merely because their spelling is identical.

column2: Yo‘q 🙂 Saqlash — keyin o‘rganish uchun yozuv qo‘shish; mastery — eslab topish va qo‘llashga oid tasdiqlangan natija. Besh so‘zni tarjimasiz eslang, gapda ishlating va keyingi kuni yana tekshiring. Coin ham faqat saqlangan son bilan tenglashtirilmaydi.
column3: No 🙂 Saving adds an item for study; mastery requires evidence of recall and use. Retrieve five words without translations, use them in sentences and check them later. Do not equate a saved-word count with verified mastery or its reward.

column2: Tanib qolishdan faol eslashga o‘ting: inglizcha izoh yoki bo‘sh gapdan so‘zni toping, o‘z gapingizni tuzing, keyin lug‘atdan tekshiring. Noto‘g‘ri bo‘lsa ma’no va birikmani tuzatib qayta eslang. Faqat ro‘yxatni qayta o‘qish yetmasligi mumkin.
column3: Move from recognition to retrieval: produce the word from a definition or gap, write your own sentence, then check the dictionary. Correct the sense or collocation and retrieve it again. Rereading alone may not solve a recall problem.

column2: Avval so‘zning inglizcha sodda izohi, rasmiy bo‘lmagan vaziyat yoki bo‘sh gapdan ma’noni eslang. Keyin gap tuzing va tarjima bilan tekshiring. Taxminni tekshirilmagan ma’no qilib saqlamang; tushunmasangiz o‘zbekcha izohdan foydalanish mumkin.
column3: Try an English definition, situation or gap before checking the Uzbek translation. Produce a sentence, then verify it. Do not store an unchecked guess as the meaning; using Uzbek for clarification remains useful.

column2: Sinonimlar barcha gapda almashmaydi: register, ma’no nozikligi va collocation farq qiladi. “Strong tea”, “heavy rain”, “make a decision”ni butun birikma sifatida o‘rganing. Lug‘atdagi mos sense va misollarni tekshirmasdan har o‘xshash tarjimani qo‘ymang.
column3: Synonyms are not interchangeable in every context. Sense, register and collocation differ. Learn strong tea, heavy rain and make a decision as phrases. Check the relevant sense and examples before substituting a word.

column2: Article lug‘ati oynasida so‘zlarni tanlang, Add to vocabulary orqali mavjud mavzuli folderni tanlang yoki mos nom bilan yangisini oching. Keyin Vocabulary’da so‘zlar va ma’nolar saqlanganini tekshiring. Papka nomi so‘z ma’nosini o‘zgartirmaydi.
column3: Choose article words, use Add to vocabulary and select an existing topic folder or name a new one. Then verify the saved items and senses in Vocabulary. A folder name does not change an item’s meaning.

column2: Avval lug‘atdan shu word familyning haqiqiy shakllarini tekshiring; har so‘z uch shaklga ega emas. Misol: “We decide together.” — Fe’l. “The decision was difficult.” — Ot. “She gave a decisive answer.” — Sifat. Har gapda yangi shaklning vazifasini ko‘ring.
